title: Silent Films Featuring Trains - University Research Project Help

commenti.body:
Wow, quite compendious! In addition to what you've got, there's some excellent train destruction in the recently-restored disaster movie The Johnstown Flood, and there's a spectacular train crash that opens The Hands of Orlac.


You already have them all, but just to be sure that I hit the sub's character limit I'll mention that I have [a Letterboxd list](https://letterboxd.com/dubiouslegacy/list/buster-keaton/detail/) ranking Buster Keaton movies by amount of train content!  (Is there a train in College? It's on your list but I don't remember one.)
Thank you for the suggestions! Regarding the train in College, it only makes a brief appearance, as you can see in this [video](https://youtu.be/T45FHGOPmZU?feature=shared&t=1369).
Ah, that is a brief appearance! I missed it entirely. Well, gonna have to take College out if the No Train Content part of my list.

The one that comes to mind is Clarence Brown's excellent The Signal Tower. In addition to being a great film with a thrilling train-centric climax, it's also got a great lost-and-found story.

Basically, for decades the only copy was a 16mm print owned by a British private collector / train fan. He considered it the greatest train movie ever and refused to share it with anyone else. But historian Kevin Brownlow kept asking him and eventually the guy left it to him after he died. 

Will let you know if any others come to mind that aren't on your list already!

Oh, your inclusion of "Ride On A Runaway Train" reminded me of this cartoon that was also released as part of the American Treasures from the New Zealand Film Archive set.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FKa39AHNRjM

Great list! Definitely add [The Valley of the Giants (1919)](https://boxd.it/mOca). It was shot in Northern California and centers on two rival logging companies with a romantic subplot between the son of one lumber baron and the daughter of the other. Part of the narrative involves the construction of a rail line and there’s some absolutely spectacular shots of lumber being transported and one very high-drama runaway train scene. 

The film itself was thought to be lost until 2010 when a print turned up in an archive in Russia. I believe it was recently restored as I saw it a couple years ago at a museum screening. Not sure about current availability (no streaming yet from what I can see), but definitely worth a watch for the train scenes alone if you can track it down.
Thank you! That sounds incredibly interesting. It's a real shame it's not available online at the moment.

I think my comment got removed because of the character limit, sorry if you read this already. Hopefully this disclaimer is enough to reach the limit, because i don't have anything more to say. Anyways...

Two more thoughts for you:

The Russian war drama The Nail In The Boot prominently features an armored train.

And you might want to look at The Railrodder, which was made well after the silent era, but it still dialogue free in the silent era style. Might be a interesting addition or footnote to all of Buster's train antics from his heyday.
